items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: I was chosen to pay tribute to Cozy Cole, who was the great drummer who played with Louis Armstrong and Cab Calloway.

ctx.x: What was the rock & roll kind of revolution? How did that kind of affect you as a drummer?

Well, it kind of affected my father a little bit more. Because around that time in let’s say early 60s around that time, he was on television until around maybe 1967 or so. Then after that, you know, he wasn’t really into it anymore. But times change and you have to go with the changes. My dad was, unfortunately, one of the guys that the rock & rollers said, “Hey old man, you know you’ve got to go to the Smithsonian Institute.” And my father still had a lot of fire in the furnace and had to play some jazz. But we…
Name some of the other — well, I could be picking up names off the floor all day with you I know – but who are some of your really favorite experiences you’ve had?
